target_customer: Infrastructure and DevOps teams at web scale companies and enterprises running containerized workloads, paying for the commercial Tectonic Kubernetes platform and support
problem: Running large server fleets required patching and managing general purpose Linux by hand; teams wanted a minimal, automatically updating OS built for containers and later a supported Kubernetes distribution.
business_model: Open source core with paid enterprise subscriptions and support (Tectonic) and managed offerings
product_category: Container-focused Linux OS and Kubernetes infrastructure tooling

founders.name: Alex Polvi
founders.background_notes: Prior startup and employer are from general knowledge of the founder and were not re-verified in this pass; the YC page gives no background.

founders.name: Brandon Philips
founders.background_notes: Named as CTO in 2015 press coverage.

competitors.name: Docker (dotCloud)
competitors.what: Container runtime that CoreOS shipped alongside, a partner more than a rival at first

competitors.name: Red Hat Project Atomic
competitors.what: Lean Docker host OS built from Fedora, CentOS or RHEL packages
competitors.traction_then: Announced April 2014, after CoreOS's first alpha

technical_complexity.rationale: A minimal immutable OS with atomic A/B updates, plus distributed systems pieces like etcd, was hard for a small team, and later work on Kubernetes distributions raised the bar further.

defensibility.rationale: Open source projects such as etcd became widely embedded in Kubernetes, but the Linux distribution itself could be matched by Red Hat and others.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Red Hat launched Project Atomic in April 2014 as a counter, and then bought CoreOS in January 2018 for 250 million dollars.

market_need_then: Container adoption and large fleets of cloud servers created demand for a lightweight, auto-updating host OS; InfoWorld in 2014 described CoreOS as a threat to Linux vendors.

branding.domain_note: Used coreos.com, which redirected to OpenShift after the acquisition.

identity.logo: A new logo was given to the Linux distribution when renamed Container Linux in 2016
identity.visual_style: Developer infrastructure style, open source projects with separate names

branding.brand_signature: Open source project names such as etcd and Tectonic

rebrands.why: To separate the company name from the Linux distribution product

branding.community_and_virality: Strong developer community around the open source projects; no merch or fan accounts found in this search.

brand_strength.rationale: Well known among infrastructure engineers and the name carried the project, but the product and company names blurred together, which forced the 2016 rename.

pivots.why: Monetize by selling an enterprise distribution built on Kubernetes

outcome_analysis: CoreOS rode the container wave with an open source OS and etcd, raised about 48 million dollars through a Series B in 2016, and moved from an OS to a commercial Kubernetes platform. Red Hat answered with Project Atomic in 2014 and eventually bought the company for 250 million dollars in January 2018, a solid but not outsized exit, to merge Tectonic into OpenShift.
notes: Seed round with a16z and Sequoia in 2013 is mentioned only by one aggregator (Seedtable) with no amount, so it is not recorded as a round. Total raised reported as 48, 50 or 53 million. Series A 8 million date is given only as 2014. The 2015 SiliconANGLE headline calls the 12 million a Series B but TechCrunch-style coverage treats it as an extension of Series A, so it is recorded as series_a. Founder prior employer detail for Alex Polvi was not confirmed in this pass.
